Apply items 1 to 12, in severity order: the HIGH items first (10, 6, 1), then MEDIUM, then LOW. Commit in small steps.

Constraints:
- Use the existing components, tokens and Tailwind conventions. Add no new dependency.
- Item 1 changes `resurgo/worker.py` and its status file. Keep the existing contract keys and only add `reason`, `queued_at` (installation) and `started` (repo entry). Extend `resurgo/test_worker.py` by the smallest case, and run `uv run --with pytest pytest -q resurgo`.
- Item 5 may need a short "Run it yourself" section in README.md. Write only what is true about running `resurgo.run`: Docker host, uv, the model gateway env var and the optional neatlogs key. Name no servers or addresses.
- Copy follows the site's voice: sentence case, verb-first buttons, no "please".
- Any motion follows docs/ANIMATION.md.

- Run `npm run build`.
- Run `web/check-render.mjs` with 360 added to its widths (360, 420 and 1280, light and dark), against the API on port 8787.
- Confirm no page-level sideways scroll at 360 on `/`, `/runs`, a run page, `/installed/<id>` and `/data`.
- Take close-ups of the How-it-works chips at 360, the gallery cards at 360, and `/installed` in its waiting state with the new reason. Look at them yourself.

Rules:
- Don't push, don't merge, and don't edit hackathon.md.
- Never read `.env` or `.entire/settings.local.json`.
- Run no `docker` commands.
- No tool or AI attribution in commits.
- Don't invent numbers, prices or promises.
- Finish with a short report: what changed per item, the check results with screenshot paths, and anything you weren't sure about.

No placeholder numbers. 16 - A section hides itself when its data is absent (no featured run, no repos, no evidence line). 17 - Run ids must match `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-`; resolved paths must stay inside `RUNS_DIR`. 18 - A run directory with no `result.json` younger than 45 minutes is listed as "Checking"; older ones are omitted. 19 - Older records use `result: fail | fixed`. They are shown as "✗ Broken" and "◐ Fixed, unverified" (written before the clean-container check existed). 20 21 ## Choices worth knowing 22 23 - **Built on** names neatlogs and Entire only. `docs/LANDING.md` also lists AWS Bedrock, but `hackathon.md` records the model as an OpenAI model behind a self-hosted gateway, so Bedrock is left off until that is true. 24 - **GitHub App**: now exists ("Resurgo Agent"); copy updated, see "Logos, copy, third status" below. The $2 pricing line is still labelled "Planned" because there is no billing. 25 - **Test-set strip** counts repos actually run, not "24". The 24-repo held-out claim waits for the sweep. 26 - **Stats trio** is computed from recorded runs (development repos) and says so. Held-out v1 vs v2 and cost per fix are not shown; no such measurement exists in the records. 27 - **Trace id**: result.json has no trace id yet, so the run view says "not recorded for this run". If the runner adds a `trace_id` field it shows up automatically. 28 - **Problem section** uses three causes found in the real records: pnpm `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`, the agent's own diagnosis of a native module vs Node 24, and a build that hit the time cap. The "build-time API host disappeared" cause in LANDING.md has no evidence in our runs, so it is not claimed. 29 - **Replay** plays the recorded steps and model calls back from `result.json`; nothing is re-executed. With `prefers-reduced-motion` it jumps straight to the verdict. 30 - **Orb**: one orb, paused unless the replay is at a model call. 31 32 ## Components 33 34 SmoothUI (via the shadcn registry): `ai-task-list`, `ai-reasoning`, `ai-diff`, `siri-orb` (+ its `ai-core`) in `src/components/smoothui/`. One colour tweak in `ai-diff` for contrast on the dark canvas. 35 36 ## Second pass: Daylight lab, choreography, agent view 37 38 - **Theme**: tokens are `docs/reference/tokens.css` verbatim in `src/index.css`. Light by default; the sun/moon toggle saves `resurgo-theme` in localStorage (try/catch) and `index.html` applies it before paint. No saved choice: the system preference decides. Logo is the brand wordmark SVG chosen by theme; no hard-coded colours remain (SmoothUI diff/task-list/orb now use tokens). 39 - **Hero** (`components/Story.tsx`, `lib/story.ts`): `frameAt(story, t)` is a pure function of time over the real run record. Windows rise over 0.6 s, 0.55 s apart; rationale streams at 35 cps (first sentence of each attempt, cut at a word if long, so it is an excerpt, not a rewrite); commands are typed with the sample's per-character variance; timers count up to the recorded durations. Loops after 4.5 s, pauses off screen, reduced motion shows the final frame. 40 - **Live tiles**: latest run per repo with its recorded status; only the spotlight (and the visible window when there are more than six repos) moves, every 3-5 s. 41 - **Chat**: input matches `owner/name` or a github.com URL against the gallery and replays that run through the same Story. No match: "Live checks open with the GitHub App." and the list of replayable repos. Nothing is invented. 42 - **Solution tabs** advance on their own (hover/focus/click holds them), stream a real excerpt, and omit any stat with no measurement. 43 - **Status fix**: `api/main.py` judges legacy `fixed`/`fail` records by their verifier steps: all passed means Runs (or Runs with gaps if the record lists gaps); "Fixed, unverified" only when there are no verifier steps. `verified` is in every summary. 44 - **/api/runs** now carries steps, attempts, rationale, error line, problem evidence and a patch preview, so the landing page fetches only the featured run's record. Records are cached by mtime. 45 - **Agent view**: `/index.md` and `/llms.txt` are generated from the live records; footer link "Agent view". 46 47 ## Third pass: motion review (docs/ANIMATION.md) 48 49 Checked against Lasseter's principles as listed in `docs/ANIMATION.md` (the PDF URL returned 404 when fetched, so the doc's list was the reference). 50 51 - **Tokens** live in `src/index.css`: `--ease-enter`, `--ease-exit`, `--ease-arc`, `--dur-chip` 150 ms, `--dur-window` 600 ms, `--blink` 400 ms. `lib/ease.ts` reads `--ease-enter` for the JS animations (SmoothUI diff and reasoning). `main.tsx` imports the CSS before the app so the token exists when it is read. Nothing else defines an entrance easing. 52 - **Windows** rise with CSS (`.win`, `data-in`), not per-frame JS: Y uses the enter easing, X the arc easing, exits are 300 ms and gentler. The title bar leads; `.win-body` follows 120 ms later. 53 - **Staging**: `buildStory` now runs strictly one beat at a time (cursor wait, typing, run, reading pause, agent thinking, agent streaming, reading pause, next command). `story.focus` says which window acts; the others dim to 0.55 and all return to full opacity 700 ms after the verdict. The agent's streamed text used to overlap the terminal's next command; it no longer does. 54 - **Anticipation**: two cursor blinks (800 ms) before each typed command; spinner and "Thinking…" in the agent window for 1.3 s before its text streams; clean-container window rises before its first tile; solution-tab indicator moves 160 ms before its content swaps; chat reply shows "Looking in the gallery…" for 450 ms before streaming. 55 - **Reading pauses** are `250 ms + 30 ms/word` (`readingMs` in `lib/stream.ts`): after a failing step's error lines, after each streamed rationale, before the chat replay takes over, in the run-view replay after a failing step, and before a solution tab advances (min 1.8 s). 56 - **Exaggeration, three places**: the failing step's row flashes red once (300 ms, `.flash-bad`), the first command that passes after the last repair gets one lemon sweep (`.sweep`), the verdict (and the replay button when it turns to its verdict) overshoots once to 1.03 (`.verdict-land`). 57 - **Lift**: when a verified run's verdict lands in a replay (hero, chat, run view) `lib/beat.ts` fires `resurgo:lift` and the header wordmark rises 4 px and settles. The whole wordmark lifts; it is an `` of the brand SVG, so the r alone can't be moved without editing the brand file. 58 - **Secondary action** pauses while a story plays (`useBeatOwner` / `data-beat` on ``): the tile spotlight timer stops, the tile dot stops pulsing. Cursor blink is only ever shown while a command waits to be typed; typed and streamed text uses a solid cursor. 59 - **Squash**: `.press` gives buttons 0.97 on press and a 150 ms return. Never applied to text blocks. 60 - **Theme toggle**: colours cross-fade 240 ms (`.theme-fade`, off under reduced motion); the icon turns in. 61 - **Route change**: the page rises in (260 ms); run-view tab panels do the same. 62 - **Reveals and icon draws** are CSS now (`lib/inview.ts`); no motion-library variants with their own easings. 63 - **Reduced motion**: stories jump to the final frame, reveals are plain, streams show full text, tab and spotlight timers do not run, and the global rule zeroes the remaining CSS durations. 64 65 Not done / limits: 66 67 - **No frame captures.** Chromium and the API server could not be started in this session (non-interactive, commands needing approval were refused), so nothing was screenshotted in either theme. If the fix was only ever proved in the clean container, no row is swept. 69 - The hero loop fades the whole story out for 350 ms before restarting; individual windows do not exit one by one. 70 - Tiles that slide along the list (more than six repos) jump to their new position; only the arriving tile animates. 71 - Wall time is compressed in the story, but every timer counts to the recorded duration and is labelled. A full run is now longer than before because of the reading pauses. 72 73 ## Fourth pass: blank landing on summary-only /api/runs 74 75 - **Crash**: `findProblems` in `pages/landing-data.ts` called `r.problems.find` on list rows. When `/api/runs` returned summary fields only (id, repo, sha, path, type, status, duration_s, model_calls, fix_kind, needs_approval, started) that threw inside the `useMemo`, and with no boundary React unmounted `#root`. `LiveTiles` read `r.verifier_steps.length` the same way. 76 - **Contract**: in `lib/api.ts` only those eleven fields are required on `RunSummary`; `type` and `fix_kind` are nullable for older records. Everything else (`verified`, `gaps`, `*_steps`, `attempts`, `problems`, `patch_preview`, …) is optional, so `tsc` flags any unguarded read. Steps and attempts come from `/api/runs/{id}` (`useRun`), which the landing already fetches for the featured run only. 77 - **Fallbacks**: verified runs are counted from `status` (`runs`, `runs_with_gaps`) when `verified` is absent. A tile's clean-container line is blank, not "none recorded", when the list has no `verifier_steps`. 78 - **Boundaries**: `components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` wraps every landing section and the route outlet. A throw shows "
could not be shown" in place and logs the error; the header, footer and other sections stay. 79 - **Known loss**: "The problem" section needs `problems` (evidence lines) and hides itself when list rows lack them. Restoring it with a summary-only list means fetching details for the failing runs; not done. 80 - **Check**: `node web/check-render.mjs [baseUrl] [runId] [shotDir]` loads `/`, `/runs` and `/runs/` with `chromium --headless=new --dump-dom` (6 s virtual time), exits 1 if `#root` has under 80 characters of text or a boundary notice, and writes light and dark screenshots. It needs the API running (it serves `web/dist`). 81 - **Not verified in the session that wrote this**: starting the API and Chromium needed an approval the non-interactive session could not get, so the script was syntax-checked (`node --check`) and the app built (`tsc -b` + `vite build`), but not run. A run is verified when the verifier ran at least one step and `verifier.passed` is true or every step exited 0; a legacy `fixed`/`fail` is then judged by those steps. "Unverified" is only for a record with no verifier steps at all. `20261010T101804Z-5c3370f` (clone, toolchain, detect, install all exit 0, `passed: true`) is verified. `20261010T093642Z-5c3370f` is not unverified: it has four verifier steps and the install exited 1 with `passed: false`, so it is Broken. 95 - **Stale API**: the process on REDACTED:8787 predates these API changes (its detail summary has no `verified` and returns `status: "fixed"`). Restart it to see the new status; the web build does not decide status. 96 - **Replay run**: sits in the "What actually ran" header row (flex, wraps under the heading on narrow widths). 97 - **check-render.mjs**: the theme labels were swapped (Blink's `preferredColorScheme` 0 is dark, 1 is light), so the "light" screenshots were dark. Fixed. 98 - **Not verified**: the status change itself in a browser, because a current API could not be started in the session that made it (server and Python execution needed an approval it could not get). The logic was checked by reading `_verified` / `_status` against both records fetched from the running API. 99 - **Seen, then fixed in the next section**: at 420 px the landing page had a page-level horizontal scrollbar, and long step output in the run view showed inner horizontal scrollbars. 100 101 ## Layout fixes, install entry point, deploy files 102 103 - **Sideways scroll at 420 px** had two sources. "Weekly re-checks" and "keeps watch" are gone (no schedules exist). 115 - **`fix_awaiting_approval`**: "Fix verified · awaiting approval", glyph ◆, dashed amber outline. `_status` returns it when `needs_approval` is true, `_verified` is true, `verifier.passed` is not false, and the record's own `result` is not `broken`. `verified` stays true (the verifier did pass), but the run view, the story and the lift flourish treat only a non-awaiting verified run as a clean pass. 1	# Motion checklist: Lasseter's principles applied to Resurgo
2	
3	Source: John Lasseter, "Principles of Traditional Animation Applied to 3D Computer Animation", SIGGRAPH 1987. PDF: https://www.ics.uci.edu/~fowlkes/class/ics162/exercises/lasseter.pdf (mirror: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/academic/class/15462-f13/www/lec_slides/Lesseter.pdf)
4	
5	**Rule for every animator (Claude, Codex, Agy):** read the paper and this list before animating anything. Afterwards, report one line per principle: what you did and where.
6	
7	1. **Squash and stretch.** Use subtle scale changes that preserve volume, only at moments of contact. Buttons compress to about 0.96 on press and settle back. The verdict chip lands with a single overshoot to about 1.03. Never squash text.
8	2. **Timing.** Duration conveys weight. Chips take 120–180 ms and windows 450–650 ms. Reading pauses scale with text length, roughly 250 ms plus 30 ms per word, so the eye can finish before the next beat. Streaming runs at about 35 characters per second. Real durations always appear as labels, even when time is compressed.
9	3. **Anticipation.** Cue each beat before it happens. The cursor blinks twice before typing starts. A window's title bar appears about 120 ms before its body. The spinner appears before output streams. A tab's indicator moves before its content swaps.
10	4. **Staging.** Run one focal action at a time. Dim inactive windows to about 0.55 opacity while another one acts. The eye path is project row, agent, terminal, clean container, verdict. Never animate the main content of two windows at once.
11	5. **Follow-through and overlapping action.** Children trail their parents: a window's content staggers 30–60 ms behind its frame. Lines settle with a 2 px overshoot. After the verdict lands, the tile row finishes moving a moment later.
12	6. **Straight-ahead versus pose-to-pose.** The story is pose-to-pose: key beats taken from the real run record (idle, failing, fixing, proving, verdict), planned first. Streaming text, timers and spinners are straight-ahead, generated as they play.
13	7. **Slow in and slow out.** Entrances share one easing, for example `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`, and exits use a gentler one. Nothing moves linearly except timers, progress and spinner rotation.
14	8. **Arcs.** Moving elements travel on slight curves (X and Y with different easings), not straight diagonals. The orb drifts on an arc.
15	9. **Exaggeration.** Push only the key moments. The failing ✗ line flashes red once for 300 ms, the winning fix line gets one quick lemon sweep, and the verdict alone gets a scale overshoot. Everything else stays calm.
16	10. **Secondary action.** It supports the main action and never competes with it. The orb breathes only while the model is thinking, the cursor blinks, timers tick, and tile status dots pulse softly. All of these pause when the primary action needs attention.
17	11. **Appeal.** Aim for clarity and personality: legible type, generous spacing, honest data and a steady rhythm. The agent should feel calm and competent, with one small flourish at the win: the lifted-r mark gives a short "lift" when a run verifies.
18	
19	Also:
20	- `prefers-reduced-motion` shows final poses only.
21	- Motion is never the only signal. Every state is a word plus a glyph.
22	- Every replay comes from a real run record. Animation never invents a result.
23	
24	## Video output quality (standing rule)
25	- Every video has a **4K master: 3840x2160**. Render web content at a 1920x1080 layout with deviceScaleFactor 2 so text stays crisp. Encode H.264 High at CRF 16 or better, yuv420p. Use 60 fps for motion-heavy pieces (30 fps is acceptable for slow ones).
26	- Platform exports come from the master, for example a high-bitrate 1080p file for X, which re-encodes uploads.
27	- Check the master with ffprobe (resolution, fps, codec) before calling it done.

2	
3	Usage: uv run python -m resurgo.worker [--once]
4	
5	The web API drops $QUEUE_DIR/requests/<installation_id>.json when someone installs the App. This
6	worker validates the request against the App, plans the checks (public repos, at most 5, at most 3
7	project paths each), runs them with the sweep's runner and reports progress in
8	$QUEUE_DIR/status/<installation_id>.json, which the web page shows. Pull requests are opened only
9	when RESURGO_AUTO_PR=1. A finished installation is re-queued once its status is a week old.
10	--once works until nothing is left to do, then exits.
11	"""
12	import argparse
13	import json
14	import os
15	import subprocess
16	import sys
17	import time
18	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
19	from pathlib import Path
20	
21	import httpx
22	from dotenv import load_dotenv

24	from resurgo import __version__
25	from resurgo.pr import api, app_jwt
26	from resurgo.run import scrub
27	from resurgo.sweep import run_one

29	RUNS = Path("runs")
30	MANIFESTS = ("package.json", "foundry.toml", "Cargo.toml")
31	MAX_REPOS, MAX_PATHS = 5, 3
32	POLL_S = 10
33	RECHECK_AFTER = timedelta(days=7)
34	RESULTS = ("runs", "runs_with_gaps", "broken", "unsupported")
35	OPEN = ("queued", "checking")

38	class GitHubError(Exception):
39	    pass
40	
41	
42	def now():
43	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
44	
45	
46	def log(line):
47	    print(line, flush=True)

50	def call(method, path, token=None, ok_404=False, **kw):
51	    """pr.api, but every failure is a GitHubError (pr.api exits the process on an error status)."""
52	    try:
53	        r = api(method, path, token, **kw)
54	    except SystemExit as e:
55	        raise GitHubError(scrub(str(e))) from None
56	    except httpx.HTTPError as e:
57	        raise GitHubError(type(e).__name__) from None
58	    if r.status_code == 404 and not ok_404:
59	        raise GitHubError(f"GitHub {method} {path.split('?')[0]} returned 404")
60	    return r

63	def make_jwt():
64	    client_id, key = os.environ.get("GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID"), os.environ.get("GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY")
65	    if not client_id or not key:
66	        raise GitHubError("GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY must be set")
67	    try:
68	        return app_jwt(client_id, key)
69	    except SystemExit as e:

73	def choose_paths(tree):
74	    """Project paths from a git tree listing: the root when it has a manifest, otherwise the
75	    first-level directories that do (at most MAX_PATHS, by name)."""
76	    blobs = [e["path"] for e in tree if e.get("type") == "blob"]
77	    if any(m in blobs for m in MANIFESTS):
78	        return [""]
79	    dirs = {p.split("/")[0] for p in blobs if p.count("/") == 1 and p.rsplit("/", 1)[1] in MANIFESTS}
80	    return sorted(dirs)[:MAX_PATHS]

83	def find_record(runs_dir, repo, sha, path, version):
84	    """The newest recorded run of this repo, SHA, path and agent version, or None."""
85	    for f in sorted(runs_dir.glob("*/result.json"), reverse=True):
86	        try:
87	            rec = json.loads(f.read_text())
88	        except (OSError, ValueError):
89	            continue
90	        if (rec.get("repo"), rec.get("sha", "")[:12], rec.get("path", ""), rec.get("agent_version")) \
91	                == (repo, sha, path, version) and rec.get("result"):
92	            return rec

96	def entry(repo, sha="", path="", state="queued", reason=""):
97	    return {"repo": repo, "sha": sha[:12], "path": path, "state": state, "reason": reason,
98	            "run_id": None, "result": None, "needs_approval": False, "pr": None}

101	def label(it):
102	    return it["repo"] + (f" ({it['path']})" if it["path"] else "")

105	def load(path):
106	    try:

108	    except (OSError, ValueError):

113	def save(queue, status):
114	    """Write the status atomically; the installation is done once no repo is queued or checking."""
115	    if status["state"] != "rejected":
116	        status["state"] = "checking" if any(i["state"] in OPEN for i in status["repos"]) else "done"
117	    status["updated"] = now()
118	    out = queue / "status"

125	def plan(repo, branch, token):
126	    """The queued entries for one public repo: a head SHA and one entry per project path."""
127	    r = call("GET", f"/repos/{repo}/branches/{branch}", token, ok_404=True)
128	    if r.status_code == 404:
129	        return [entry(repo, state="skipped", reason="empty repository")]
130	    full = r.json()["commit"]["sha"]
131	    tree = call("GET", f"/repos/{repo}/git/trees/{full}", token, params={"recursive": "1"}).json()["tree"]
132	    paths = choose_paths(tree)

134	        return [entry(repo, full, state="skipped", reason="no package.json, foundry.toml or Cargo.toml")]

138	def intake(queue, request, installation_id):
139	    """Validate a request with the App and write its status. Raises GitHubError, leaving the
140	    request in place, when GitHub cannot answer."""
141	    jwt = make_jwt()
142	    r = call("GET", f"/app/installations/{installation_id}", jwt, ok_404=True)
143	    if r.status_code == 404:

174	    found = []

183	    files = [f for f in (queue / "status").glob("*.json") if f.stem.isdigit()]
